## 2. The flow view

`/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/web/src/components/FlowView.tsx` (714 lines) — the whole thing.

**Data it renders.** Two fetches on mount (161-167):
- `api.flow()` → `GET /api/flow` → `IntegrationDetail[]` (scaffold records + dapr components + pipeline step filenames).
- `api.topologies()` → `GET /api/topology` → `TopologyReport { topologies: Topology[], errors?: string[] }`.

The declared topology is the **only** source of nodes and edges. `/api/flow` is used *only* to (a) build the system dropdown with counts, and (b) join a declared component name to a scaffolded integration path so clicking selects it (`nodeId` map, 398-407). Comment at 218-219 is explicit: "Only a declared topology is drawn — there is no inferred fallback." A system with no record renders the empty state (299-304).

**Schema (`topology.intropy.io/v1`, kind `SystemTopology`).** Go: `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/topology/topology.go`; mirrored TS: `web/src/api.ts:232-373`.

```
Entry { path }            // root-relative system dir, injected by the CLI (handlers.go:322)
Topology {
  apiVersion, kind, system
  components[] { name, kind, subscribes[]{pubsub,topic}, publishes[]{pubsub,topic},
                 ports[]{port, direction:"in"|"out"}, provides[], consumes[] /*opaque json.RawMessage*/ }
  topics[]    { pubsub, topic, contract?, publishers[], subscribers[] }   // lookup table
  ports[]     { name, externalSystem?, directions[], usedBy[] }          // lookup table
  contracts[] { name, kind, shortName, mediaType, fingerprint, schema /*raw JSON Schema*/ }
  apis[]      // opaque
  messageDocs?: Record<portName, MessageDoc>   // CLI-merged, NOT host-declared
}
```
Wiring is **inline edges on each component** — there is no top-level edge list. `topics[]`/`ports[]` are metadata tables the inline refs resolve against. Anything opaque (`apis`, `provides`, `consumes`) is `json.RawMessage` passed through unrendered because the shape isn't final (topology.go:46-50).

1. Build `topicMeta` / `portMeta` lookup maps (387-390).
2. Node IDs: component → matched integration path if a scaffold exists, else `component:<name>` (402-407); topic → `topic:<pubsub>/<topic>` (393).
3. Collect unique topic refs and internal flow edges from inline `publishes`/`subscribes` (411-425).
4. **Longest-path layering** (Kahn relaxation, 431-457) over internal edges → `depth` map = column index. Cycles land in column 0 rather than failing.

7. Edges (530-559): publish = component `ext` handle (right) → topic `in`; subscribe = topic `out` → component `in`. All with `MarkerType.ArrowClosed` and `className:'rf-edge-ext'`.
8. Externals (ports) sit **outside** the group (566-623): direction `in` → placed left of its component; direction `out` → stacked below the component's column via `belowY(col)`. Deliberate to avoid whole-diagram crossings (comment 561-565).

## 3. How the dashboard gets its data

All HTTP JSON, `fetch` from `web/src/api.ts:375-425`. **No websockets, no SSE, no background polling.** Route table — `internal/dashboard/handlers.go:138-157`:

| Route | Handler | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | `health` (160) | `{status, version}` |
| `GET /api/integrations` | `listIntegrations` (171) | mirrors `int list -o json` + derived name/system/domain/systemPath |
| `GET /api/integrations/{path...}` | `getIntegration` (404) | + AGENTS.md/README.md/dapr components/pipeline steps |
| `GET /api/catalog/{path...}` | `catalog` (catalog.go:98) | never blocks; answers `pending` and calls `warmTopologies()` |
| `GET /api/flow` | `flow` (265) | all integrations + components + pipeline steps in one shot |
| `GET /api/topology` | `topologies` (284) | cached provider result |
| **`POST /api/topology/refresh`** | `refreshTopologies` (290) | re-runs every host's graph verb |
| `GET /api/deploy/{path...}` | `getDeployState` (416) | runs `deploy status` on first ask, then cached |
| **`POST /api/deploy/{path...}`** | `refreshDeployState` (422) | re-run |
| `GET /api/templates` | `listTemplates` (templates.go:77) | |
| `GET /api/templates/{name}` | `getTemplate` (100) | |
| **`POST /api/templates/{name}/create`** | `createTemplate` (127) | **writes files** |
| `/` | static SPA | |

**Caching model** (`apiServer`, handlers.go:46-74):
- `topoMu` / `topoLoaded` / `topoEntries` / `topoErrs`: the topology is computed **once, lazily on first request**, because it runs `dotnet build` + `dotnet run -- graph` per host. `cachedTopologies(ctx, force)` (315). `warmTopologies()` (348) computes in a detached goroutine so the catalog endpoint never queues behind a build.
- `depMu` / `depStates map[path]deployState`: per-integration, `deployStateTimeout = 1 minute` (43) — the bound exists to release the shared GitOps checkout lock, not for the browser.
- `createMu`: serializes create runs (two renders of the same name would race, and each downloads a tarball).
- Message docs are re-read from disk **on every request** (`topologyReport`, 298-310), so editing a `messages/*.md` shows up on browser refresh without re-running graph verbs.

The only client-side timer: `Catalog.tsx:33-34` `PENDING_RETRY_MS = 5000`, `PENDING_RETRY_CAP = 36` — retries a `topologyPending` catalog entry for up to 3 minutes while the background build finishes. Nothing else polls (deliberate; README lines ~950-957 explain why a background poll would deadlock the user's own `intropy deploy`).

**Topology provider** — `internal/dashboard/topology.go:25-42`: `hostGraphProvider(root)` → `template.ListSystemHosts(root)` → `topology.RunGraph(ctx, hostDir)` per host; `Entry.Path = filepath.Dir(h.Path)` (the system dir, since components are siblings of the host). Policy: never fail, report per host into `errs`. `topology.RunGraph` (`internal/topology/graph.go:28`) does `dotnet build` then `dotnet run --no-build --no-launch-profile --project <hostDir> -- graph`, decodes stdout, `GraphTimeout = 5 * time.Minute`. `Decode` rejects any other `apiVersion` outright (topology.go:136-146).

**This already exists end-to-end.** The dashboard has a working template-create surface — the "Templates" tab.

**A flow-view create UI is mostly a re-composition job:** `FormField`/`Field` + `api.createTemplate` + the `POST /api/templates/{name}/create` endpoint already do the work. What's missing for creating *into a system from the canvas*:
1. `resolveCreate` confines output to `root/<single-segment>` — a component created inside a system needs `root/<systemPath>/<name>`, so that constraint must be relaxed (carefully) to a validated multi-segment path under root.
2. No endpoint runs `sys create` (re-assembling the host after adding a component), and no endpoint re-runs the graph verb for a single host.

## 5. Existing write/POST endpoints

Three, all in `newHandler` (handlers.go:138-157):

1. **`POST /api/topology/refresh`** — re-runs graph verbs. Writes nothing to disk (runs `dotnet build`).
2. **`POST /api/deploy/{path...}`** — re-runs `deploy status`. Refreshes a shared GitOps checkout under an exclusive lock; read-only w.r.t. the workspace.
3. **`POST /api/templates/{name}/create`** — **the only endpoint that writes files.** Renders a skeleton + its dependencies into the workspace and writes `.intropy/scaffold.json`.

There is no auth, no CSRF token, and no `Origin` check — the server binds `127.0.0.1` by default (`dashboard.go:47`) and that is the entire threat model. Something to weigh if the create surface grows.

## 6. `scaffold.json` record format

`/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/template/scaffold.go:61-92`. Written by `RunCreate` (prepare.go:128-141) / `Create` (create.go:124-137) to **`<projectRoot>/.intropy/scaffold.json`** (`ScaffoldRelPath`, line 18), `ScaffoldSchemaVersion = 1`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "template": "hello-world",          // library DIRECTORY name, not metadata.name — what a re-fetch needs
  "owner": "integrio-intropy",
  "repo": "intropy-templates",
  "version": "v0.4.1",                // resolved release tag, never "latest"
  "values": { "name": "...", "...": "..." },   // the fully resolved render values
  "role": "system-host",              // omitempty; from intropy.dev/template-role
  "blockKind": "extractor",           // omitempty; from intropy.dev/block-kind
  "dataFlow": "in",                   // omitempty; from intropy.dev/data-flow
  "dependsOn": [ { "template": "shared-models", "dir": "../Acme.Models" } ]
}
```

`dir` is slash-separated, relative to the component root. Note it carries **no `outputDir`** — the file's own location *is* the project root (comment 57-60). Helpers: `WriteScaffold` (107), `LoadScaffold` (124), `FindScaffold(startDir)` (139, walks up; `ErrScaffoldNotFound`). This record is the join key for everything: `sys create` assembles from it, the dashboard sidebar/catalog groups by it, and a component's *directory name* is what joins it to its topology `components[].name` (catalog.go:185-192, FlowView.tsx:398-407).

## What we're working with

- The flow view is a **React Flow** canvas (`web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`) that renders **only declared topology** — the JSON each system host emits from its `graph` verb (`dotnet run -- graph`). Nodes/edges are laid out deterministically; the canvas is strictly read-only today (no `onConnect`, no edit affordances).
- **Creation machinery already exists end-to-end**: the Templates tab posts to `POST /api/templates/{name}/create`, which runs `template.PrepareCreate`/`RunCreate` and writes the scaffold. The form renderer (`FormField` in `TemplatesView.tsx`) is generic over template `FieldSpec`s and directly reusable.
- Templates already carry `intropy.dev/block-kind` and `data-flow` labels, so a create-UI can offer "extractor / loader / transactional" as canvas-native concepts without new metadata.
- The key architectural tension: **the canvas draws truth derived from compiled hosts, but creating a component only writes a scaffold.** A new component won't appear in the declared topology until `sys create` re-assembles the host and the graph verb re-runs (a `dotnet build`, minutes not milliseconds). Every design below has to represent that gap honestly.

## Design directions

**A. Palette + drop, form in a drawer (the "diagramming tool" feel).** A left-hand palette of block kinds (filtered by template labels). Drag one into a system group; on drop, a side drawer opens with the existing template form, pre-filled with system context (name prefix, system path). Submit → existing create endpoint → the node renders immediately as a **ghost/draft node** ("scaffolded, not yet in topology") until a refresh confirms it. Most conventional and discoverable; medium effort. Main backend change: relax `resolveCreate` to allow validated multi-segment output paths (`root/<systemPath>/<name>`), plus serving labels on the template list endpoint.

**B. Connect-first ("draw the wire, get the right form").** Enable dragging a connection from a topic's out-handle (or a port) onto empty canvas. The gesture itself carries intent — "I want a subscriber to this topic" — so the UI can pre-filter templates by data-flow direction and pre-fill topic/pubsub/contract parameters. This is the most "flow-native" interaction and plays to your model where wiring is derived from scaffold values at `sys create` time. It's also the most work, and it only pays off if templates actually expose topic/connector choices as parameters the form can pre-fill.

**C. Draft mode with plan/apply (terraform-style).** A toggle switches the canvas into edit mode where you place several draft nodes and sketch edges purely client-side. A panel accumulates the pending creates as a reviewable list; "Apply" runs them sequentially, then triggers `sys create` re-assembly and one topology refresh at the end. This matches the reality that topology refresh is expensive (you batch it once instead of per-component) and fits your deterministic, records-never-lie ethos — the canvas never pretends a draft is real. Highest concept cost, but the best fit if creating a system usually means adding 3–5 components in one sitting, not one.

**D. Minimal contextual "+" (cheapest experiment).** No drag-drop at all: an "add component" button in the system group header or toolbar opens the existing template form pre-scoped to that system. The canvas stays read-only; you just remove the tab-switch friction. Almost pure re-composition of existing pieces — a good first experiment to validate the pre-fill and pending-node plumbing before investing in gestures.

**Common to all of them** (worth building once, regardless of direction): ghost-node rendering for scaffolded-but-not-yet-declared components (the join logic already exists — the flow view already matches scaffold dirs to topology component names), a way to trigger host re-assembly (`sys create` has no dashboard endpoint yet), and the multi-segment path validation in `resolveCreate`.

My take: **D is the right first experiment** (a day-ish of work, validates the whole pipeline), with **A as the destination** and C's batch-apply idea worth stealing if refresh latency proves annoying. B is beautiful but should wait until template parameters actually express wiring.

What do you think about having placeholders that you can click on a map? Like having an extractor placeholder on the left, the core blocks in the middle and loader placeholders to the right?

I think it's a strong idea — arguably better than the generic drag-drop palette, and it happens to fit this codebase unusually well. Here's why, and where the design decisions are.

## Why placeholder slots fit

**The left/middle/right semantics already exist in the metadata.** The flow view has a `KIND_DATA_FLOW` map (extractor→in, transactional→both, loader→out) used today only for card glyphs, and templates carry `intropy.dev/block-kind` + `intropy.dev/data-flow` labels. So a clicked placeholder knows exactly which templates to offer: the left slot filters the library to `block-kind: extractor`, the right slot to `loader`, the middle to `transactional-integration`. Zero new metadata needed — the placeholders make existing labels spatial.

**The layout engine cooperates.** Columns are assigned by longest-path layering, and `place(depth)` just takes the next free row in a column. A placeholder is one more node appended at the bottom of its column — no layout surgery. Extractors naturally land in column 0 and loaders at the end already, so the placeholders sit where their kind's real nodes live.

**It teaches the golden path.** This is the part I like most: an empty system stops being a blank "no topology" message and becomes the archetype's shape — in → process → out with three clickable slots. The canvas itself communicates "an integration looks like this, fill in the blanks," which is very aligned with Intropy's opinionated-blueprint model. Drag-drop says "arrange whatever you want"; slots say "here's the pattern."

**It sidesteps drag-drop entirely.** Click placeholder → side drawer opens with the existing template form (the `FormField` renderer from the Templates tab), pre-filtered to that block kind and pre-scoped to the system. On submit, the placeholder itself becomes the ghost node ("scaffolded, awaiting topology") — a clean lifecycle: slot → ghost → confirmed node.

## The design decisions this raises

1. **Always visible vs. edit mode.** Always-on placeholders add noise when you're using the flow view for monitoring/reading. Options: a subtle "+" slot per column that's low-contrast until hover; or an explicit "add components" toggle that reveals the slots. I lean toward the subtle always-on version for the experiment — a mode toggle is one more concept, and dashed low-contrast slots are a well-understood idiom.

2. **One slot per column vs. slot-per-gap.** Simplest: one placeholder at the bottom of each of the three kind-columns. Fancier: placeholders between existing nodes implying wiring position — but wiring is derived from scaffold values at `sys create` time, not from canvas position, so positional slots would imply something the system doesn't honor. One-per-column is honest.

3. **Middle column contents.** With minimal topology scope, middle = transactional (aggregator is cut). If multiple kinds ever map there, the middle slot's drawer just lists more templates — the design absorbs that.

4. **The empty-system case** is where this shines — but note today the flow view only renders systems that have a declared topology. Showing the slot skeleton for a system that has scaffolds but no host yet (or nothing at all) would need the system picker to include scaffold-only systems. Worth including — it's the best onboarding moment.

The host re-sync question from before still stands: after a slot-create, does the dashboard run `sys create` + topology refresh automatically, or show the ghost with a "refresh to declare" prompt?

# Flow view: create components via placeholder slots

## Context

The dashboard's flow view (`web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`) is a read-only React Flow canvas rendering declared topology from each system host's `graph` verb. Creation lives in a separate Templates tab. This experiment converts the flow view into a create surface using **placeholder slots**: subtle, always-visible dashed slot nodes — extractor on the left column, transactional ("core") in the middle, loader on the right — that open a pre-filtered create drawer when clicked. The slot arrangement makes the golden-path shape (in → process → out) visible, and an empty system renders as a fillable skeleton instead of a "no topology" message.

Decisions made with the user:
- **Slots are subtle always-on** (low-contrast dashed, brighten on hover) — no edit-mode toggle.
- **Host re-sync is manual with a prompt**: after a create, the new component renders as a *ghost node* (scaffolded, not yet declared) plus a banner showing the `intropy sys create` hint and a "Refresh topology" button. No auto-run of `sys create` in this experiment.
- **Scaffold-only / host-only systems appear in the picker** and render as the three-slot skeleton plus ghosts.

Everything reuses the existing create pipeline: `POST /api/templates/{name}/create` → `template.PrepareCreate`/`RunCreate` (`internal/dashboard/templates.go`, `internal/template/prepare.go`), and the form renderer `FormField`/`Field` from `web/src/components/TemplatesView.tsx`. Template labels `intropy.dev/block-kind` / `intropy.dev/data-flow` (constants in `internal/template/scaffold.go:24-53`) drive slot→template filtering — no new metadata.

## Phase 1 — Backend: create into a system directory

**`internal/dashboard/templates.go`**

1. Add optional `Dir string` to `createRequest` (root-relative, slash-separated; `""`/`"."` = workspace root, byte-for-byte today's behavior).
2. Extend `resolveCreate` (lines 182-219), keeping its security posture:
   - `Name` rule unchanged (single segment, no `/` `\` `.` `..`).
   - Split `Dir` on `/`; reject empty segments, `.`, `..`, segments starting with `.`, any `\`.
   - `outputDir = filepath.Join(s.root, filepath.FromSlash(dir), req.Name)`; keep the absolute-equality escape assertion generalized over the segments.
   - The dir must `os.Stat` as an existing directory under root → 422 otherwise. Do **not** require a known system scaffold in it (would block first-block-into-hand-made-dir; writes are confined under root regardless).
   - No response change: `result.OutputDir` already goes through `s.relPath`, giving the client the `/api/flow` identifier space it needs for the ghost join.
3. `listTemplates` (line 77): after `lib.List()`, loop `lib.Describe(name)` (cheap — local reads on the extracted tarball) and add an **additive** `entries` array of `{name, title, description, labels}`; keep `templates` untouched. Skip (don't 502) a template whose Describe fails.

**`internal/dashboard/handlers.go`**

4. New `GET /api/systems` handler reusing `scan()`'s systems map (which already sees `RoleSystemHost` scaffolds it filters from integration listings) → `[{path, name}]` sorted, always an array. This surfaces host-only systems (zero blocks) to the picker.

**Tests** (`internal/dashboard/templates_test.go` etc., following existing `testHandlerWith`/`writeScaffoldRole`/`postJSON` patterns):
- Happy path: create into pre-existing `acme/erp`, assert 201 + `outputDir == "acme/erp/orders"` + files on disk.
- Table-driven dir validation: `"../x"`, `"a/../b"`, `"/etc"`, `"a\\b"`, `"a//b"`, `".hidden/x"`, missing dir (422), `"."` (≡ omitted); assert nothing lands outside root.
- Labels present in `entries`; `GET /api/systems` with host-only scaffold and with empty workspace.

## Phase 2 — Frontend plumbing (no visual change)

- **`web/src/api.ts`**: `dir?: string` on `CreateRequest`; `entries?: TemplateSummary[]` (`{name, title?, description?, labels?}`) on the template list type; `SystemInfo {path, name}` + `api.systems()`.

## Phase 3 — FlowView: slots, ghosts, skeleton systems

All in `web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`, inside/around `buildDeclaredGraph` (lines 379-626).

- **Columns**: after depth assignment, `effCols = max(cols, 3)` so thin/empty graphs get a 3-column skeleton (`groupWidth`, `rowsInCol` use `effCols`). Slot columns: extractor → 0; loader → `max(2, maxDepth)`; transactional → clamped middle (`min(loaderCol-1, max(1, round(loaderCol/2)))`). Ghosts map by scaffold `blockKind`: `extractor`→left, `loader`→right, else middle.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/robinhultman/.claude/skills/golang-cli

**Persona:** You are a Go CLI engineer. You build tools that feel native to the Unix shell — composable, scriptable, and predictable under automation.

**Modes:**

- **Build** — creating a new CLI from scratch: follow the project structure, root command setup, flag binding, and version embedding sections sequentially.
- **Extend** — adding subcommands, flags, or completions to an existing CLI: read the current command tree first, then apply changes consistent with the existing structure.
- **Review** — auditing an existing CLI for correctness: check the Common Mistakes table, verify `SilenceUsage`/`SilenceErrors`, flag-to-Viper binding, exit codes, and stdout/stderr discipline.

# Go CLI Best Practices

Use Cobra + Viper as the default stack for Go CLI applications. Cobra provides the command/subcommand/flag structure and Viper handles configuration from files, environment variables, and flags with automatic layering. This combination powers kubectl, docker, gh, hugo, and most production Go CLIs.

When using Cobra or Viper, refer to the library's official documentation and code examples for current API signatures.

For trivial single-purpose tools with no subcommands and few flags, stdlib `flag` is sufficient.

## Quick Reference

| Concern             | Package / Tool                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Commands & flags    | `github.com/spf13/cobra`             |
| Configuration       | `github.com/spf13/viper`             |
| Flag parsing        | `github.com/spf13/pflag` (via Cobra) |
| Colored output      | `github.com/fatih/color`             |
| Table output        | `github.com/olekukonko/tablewriter`  |
| Interactive prompts | `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` |
| Version injection   | `go build -ldflags`                  |
| Distribution        | `goreleaser`                         |

## Project Structure

Organize CLI commands in `cmd/myapp/` with one file per command. Keep `main.go` minimal — it only calls `Execute()`.

```
myapp/
├── cmd/
│   └── myapp/
│       ├── main.go              # package main, only calls Execute()
│       ├── root.go              # Root command + Viper init
│       ├── serve.go             # "serve" subcommand
│       ├── migrate.go           # "migrate" subcommand
│       └── version.go           # "version" subcommand
├── go.mod
└── go.sum
```

`main.go` should be minimal — see [assets/examples/main.go](assets/examples/main.go).

## Root Command Setup

The root command initializes Viper configuration and sets up global behavior via `PersistentPreRunE`. See [assets/examples/root.go](assets/examples/root.go).

Key points:

- `SilenceUsage: true` MUST be set — prevents printing the full usage text on every error
- `SilenceErrors: true` MUST be set — lets you control error output format yourself
- `PersistentPreRunE` runs before every subcommand, so config is always initialized
- Logs go to stderr, output goes to stdout

## Subcommands

Add subcommands by creating separate files in `cmd/myapp/` and registering them in `init()`. See [assets/examples/serve.go](assets/examples/serve.go) for a complete subcommand example including command groups.

## Flags

See [assets/examples/flags.go](assets/examples/flags.go) for all flag patterns:

### Persistent vs Local

- **Persistent** flags are inherited by all subcommands (e.g., `--config`)
- **Local** flags only apply to the command they're defined on (e.g., `--port`)

### Required Flags

Use `MarkFlagRequired`, `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive`, and `MarkFlagsOneRequired` for flag constraints.

### Flag Validation with RegisterFlagCompletionFunc

Provide completion suggestions for flag values.

### Always Bind Flags to Viper

This ensures `viper.GetInt("port")` returns the flag value, env var `MYAPP_PORT`, or config file value — whichever has highest precedence.

## Argument Validation

Cobra provides built-in validators for positional arguments. See [assets/examples/args.go](assets/examples/args.go) for both built-in and custom validation examples.

| Validator                   | Description                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `cobra.NoArgs`              | Fails if any args provided           |
| `cobra.ExactArgs(n)`        | Requires exactly n args              |
| `cobra.MinimumNArgs(n)`     | Requires at least n args             |
| `cobra.MaximumNArgs(n)`     | Allows at most n args                |
| `cobra.RangeArgs(min, max)` | Requires between min and max         |
| `cobra.ExactValidArgs(n)`   | Exactly n args, must be in ValidArgs |

## Configuration with Viper

Viper resolves configuration values in this order (highest to lowest precedence):

1. **CLI flags** (explicit user input)
2. **Environment variables** (deployment config)
3. **Config file** (persistent settings)
4. **Defaults** (set in code)

See [assets/examples/config.go](assets/examples/config.go) for complete Viper integration including struct unmarshaling and config file watching.

### Example Config File (.myapp.yaml)

```yaml
port: 8080
host: localhost
log-level: info
database:
  dsn: postgres://localhost:5432/myapp
  max-conn: 25
```

With the setup above, these are all equivalent:

- Flag: `--port 9090`
- Env var: `MYAPP_PORT=9090`
- Config file: `port: 9090`

## Version and Build Info

Version SHOULD be embedded at compile time using `ldflags`. See [assets/examples/version.go](assets/examples/version.go) for the version command and build instructions.

## Exit Codes

Exit codes MUST follow Unix conventions:

| Code  | Meaning           | When to Use                               |
| ----- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| 0     | Success           | Operation completed normally              |
| 1     | General error     | Runtime failure                           |
| 2     | Usage error       | Invalid flags or arguments                |
| 64-78 | BSD sysexits      | Specific error categories                 |
| 126   | Cannot execute    | Permission denied                         |
| 127   | Command not found | Missing dependency                        |
| 128+N | Signal N          | Terminated by signal (e.g., 130 = SIGINT) |

See [assets/examples/exit_codes.go](assets/examples/exit_codes.go) for a pattern mapping errors to exit codes.

## I/O Patterns

See [assets/examples/output.go](assets/examples/output.go) for all I/O patterns:

- **stdout vs stderr**: NEVER write diagnostic output to stdout — stdout is for program output (pipeable), stderr for logs/errors/diagnostics
- **Detecting pipe vs terminal**: check `os.ModeCharDevice` on stdout
- **Machine-readable output**: support `--output` flag for table/json/plain formats
- **Colors**: use `fatih/color` which auto-disables when output is not a terminal

## Signal Handling

Signal handling MUST use `signal.NotifyContext` to propagate cancellation through context. See [assets/examples/signal.go](assets/examples/signal.go) for graceful HTTP server shutdown.

## Shell Completions

Cobra generates completions for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell automatically. See [assets/examples/completion.go](assets/examples/completion.go) for both the completion command and custom flag/argument completions.

## Testing CLI Commands

Test commands by executing them programmatically and capturing output. See [assets/examples/cli_test.go](assets/examples/cli_test.go).

Use `cmd.OutOrStdout()` and `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` in commands (instead of `os.Stdout` / `os.Stderr`) so output can be captured in tests.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Writing to `os.Stdout` directly | Tests can't capture output. Use `cmd.OutOrStdout()` which tests can redirect to a buffer |
| Calling `os.Exit()` inside `RunE` | Cobra's error handling, deferred functions, and cleanup code never run. Return an error, let `main()` decide |
| Not binding flags to Viper | Flags won't be configurable via env/config. Call `viper.BindPFlag` for every configurable flag |
| Missing `viper.SetEnvPrefix` | `PORT` collides with other tools. Use a prefix (`MYAPP_PORT`) to namespace env vars |
| Logging to stdout | Unix pipes chain stdout — logs corrupt the data stream for the next program. Logs go to stderr |
| Printing usage on every error | Full help text on every error is noise. Set `SilenceUsage: true`, save full usage for `--help` |
| Config file required | Users without a config file get a crash. Ignore `viper.ConfigFileNotFoundError` — config should be optional |
| Not using `PersistentPreRunE` | Config initialization must happen before any subcommand. Use root's `PersistentPreRunE` |
| Hardcoded version string | Version gets out of sync with tags. Inject via `ldflags` at build time from git tags |
| Not supporting `--output` format | Scripts can't parse human-readable output. Add JSON/table/plain for machine consumption |

## Related Skills

See `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-project-layout`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-dependency-injection`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-testing`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-design-patterns` skills.

I've read your implementation — nice contract (baseline from the host record, orphan diff, record rewritten last, conflicts refuse). My recommendation: **yes, wire it into the dashboard, but as the banner's one-click action rather than automatically inside every create.** Here's the reasoning:

**Why not auto-per-create:**

1. **Cost per click.** `Update` re-fetches the template tarball (network), re-renders the host, and `warnTopologyDrift` runs a dotnet build as its advisory check. Folding that into the create request makes every drawer submit slow and adds network/build failure modes to an action that's currently fast and local. And the canvas *still* shows a ghost afterward — wiring only appears after a topology refresh — so the user gains nothing visible for the wait.
2. **Batching.** Sketching a system usually means adding 2–3 blocks in a sitting. Auto mode does three host re-renders and three tarball downloads; a banner button folds all orphans in one pass — that's exactly the orphan-diff shape `planUpdate` already has.
3. **Failure honesty.** "Component created, host update failed" inside one request is a muddy response. Your own design is careful about honest baselines and refusing conflicts — keeping the two writes as two visible actions preserves that.
4. **The onboarding path breaks.** `planUpdate` requires an existing host — but the flow we just built lets you create the *first* block in an empty workspace or a system with no host yet. Auto-update would error on exactly the golden-path case; that situation needs `sys create`, not `sys update`.

**What I'd build instead:**

- `POST /api/systems/{path...}/update` → `system.Update` with `StartDir = root/<systemPath>` and captured stderr. One important detail from your implementation: `planUpdate` demands *exactly one* host under StartDir, so the endpoint must pass the system directory, never the workspace root (a multi-system workspace would error). The flow view's system key is already exactly that directory.
- The ghost banner becomes actionable: when the selected system has a host, "N scaffolded components not in the declared topology — **[Update host & refresh]**", which calls the update endpoint and then the existing topology refresh, so ghosts turn into declared, wired nodes in one click. When there's no host yet, keep the current `sys create` hint (a create-host button can be a follow-up).
- Serialize it with `createMu` like template creates, and map `ErrNoOrphans` to a friendly no-op.

Auto mode could still come later as an opt-in ("re-assemble after every create"), but I'd start explicit — it matches the plan/apply batching, and one click closes the whole loop.

130			Force:         opts.Force,
131			NoInput:       true, // the template's values come from the payload, never prompts
132			OnManifest:    requireFactsPayload,
133			Stdin:         strings.NewReader(""),
134			Stdout:        opts.Stdout,
135			Stderr:        opts.Stderr,
136			HTTP:          opts.HTTP,
137			UserAgent:     opts.UserAgent,
138			Owner:         opts.Owner,
139			Repo:          opts.Repo,
140			GitHubBaseURL: opts.GitHubBaseURL,
141		}); err != nil {
142			return err
143		}
144	
145		// The template derives projectName/systemClass from the name; reading
146		// them back from the record it just wrote keeps the result summary
147		// honest about what was rendered.
148		record, err := template.LoadScaffold(filepath.Join(opts.OutputDir, filepath.FromSlash(template.ScaffoldRelPath)))
149		if err != nil {
150			return err
151		}
152		hostEntry := template.ScaffoldEntry{Path: opts.OutputDir, Scaffold: *record}
153		if model.ProjectName, err = stringValue(hostEntry, "projectName"); err != nil {
154			return fmt.Errorf("template %s did not derive the host project name: %w", hostTemplate, err)
155		}
156		if model.SystemClass, err = stringValue(hostEntry, "systemClass"); err != nil {
157			return fmt.Errorf("template %s did not derive the system class name: %w", hostTemplate, err)
158		}

160		contracts := "no contracts project"
161		if model.Shared != nil {

163		}

166

168	}

171	// the facts-only payload: one that still requires sharedContracts consumes
172	// the pre-join payload shape (CLI-derived field identifiers and a csproj
173	// include path), which this CLI no longer produces. The gate runs before any
174	// output is written so an old release fails loudly instead of rendering a
175	// host that cannot compile.
176	func requireFactsPayload(t *template.Template) error {
177		required, _ := t.Spec.Parameters["required"].([]any)

181			}
182		}
183		return nil
184	}

186	// sharedPath reports the detected contracts sibling for the JSON summary;
187	// empty when the workspace has none.
188	func sharedPath(m *Model) string {
189		if m.Shared == nil {
190			return ""
191		}
192		return m.Shared.Path
193	}

Done — the endpoint and banner button are built, and the full loop is verified end-to-end, including your mid-turn addition: **when the system has no host yet, the button runs `sys create` instead.**

**Backend** (`internal/dashboard/systems.go`): `POST /api/systems/{path...}` re-assembles one system's host the way the CLI would. It branches on `template.ListSystemHosts(dir)`: a host present → `system.Update` (your new orphan-fold, honoring the record's template pin); none → `system.Create` with the system named after its directory (the same rule that labels the pseudo-system) and the host rendered inside it as `<name>-host`. The path is validated with the same segment rules as create's `dir` and must exist; runs are serialized with `createMu`. The response says which verb ran (`action: update | create | none` — "none" is `ErrNoOrphans`, a successful no-op), plus `added`/`kept` and the command's stderr as diagnostics. Errors map to 409 (divergence, retryable with force), 422 (workspace-shape problems), 502 (template fetch). Three handler tests cover the no-orphans path, the create branch's pre-network validation, and encoded traversal (raw `../` never reaches the handler — the mux 307-normalizes it).

**Frontend**: the ghost banner's passive hint became the action. It reads "N scaffolded components are not in the declared topology yet" with a button labeled **Update host & refresh** or **Create host & refresh** depending on whether `/api/systems` knows a host there. One click: sync → topology refresh → ghosts become declared, wired nodes. After a create-branch sync it also re-fetches the flow and follows the selection onto the new system key, since a new host changes every sibling's grouping key (I hit that live — it briefly produced a duplicate picker entry before the fix).

The catalog view also went from "identity from scaffold record" to a fully declared entry with contracts.
